\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق} (ra'd-o barq)}{رعد و برق (ra'd-o barq)}]{\fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق} (ra'd-o barq) — a thunderstorm; thunder and lightning}

\label{lesson:FA-C475-rad-o-barq}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to stop, then the Persian for floodwater.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق}}
\textbf{\fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق}} (\emph{ra'd-o barq}) — \textquotedblleft{}a thunderstorm; thunder and lightning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق} \fa{شدیدی} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dishab ra'd-o barq-e shadidi bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night there was a heavy thunderstorm.
\end{quote}

\emph{ra'd} 'thunder' + \emph{o} 'and' + \emph{barq} 'lightning'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ra'd-o barq} joins two Arabic loans with Persian \emph{o} 'and': \emph{ra'd} from Arabic \emph{raʿd} 'thunder' and \emph{barq} from Arabic \emph{barq} 'flashing, lightning' (EtymDB lists both).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ra'd-o barq}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ra'd-o barq}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ra'd-o barq}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to stop, then the Persian for floodwater, then say \emph{ra'd-o barq} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{رعد} \fa{و} \fa{برق} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A thunderstorm; thunder and lightning\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{صاعقه} (sâ'eqe)}{صاعقه (sâ'eqe)}]{\fa{صاعقه} (sâ'eqe) — a lightning strike, a thunderbolt}

\label{lesson:FA-C475-saeqe}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for floodwater, then the Persian for a thunderstorm.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{صاعقه}}
\textbf{\fa{صاعقه}} (\emph{sâ'eqe}) — \textquotedblleft{}a lightning strike, a thunderbolt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{صاعقه} \fa{به} \fa{درخت} \fa{بلند} \fa{حیاط} \fa{خورد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Sâ'eqe be derakht-e boland-e hayât khord.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Lightning struck the tall tree in the courtyard.
\end{quote}

\emph{Sâ'eqe zad} — lightning struck.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{sâ'eqe} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ṣāʿiqa}, which EtymDB lists; it is usually glossed 'a thunderbolt'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sâ'eqe}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{sâ'eqe}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for floodwater, then the Persian for a thunderstorm, then say \emph{sâ'eqe} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{غرش} \fa{کردن} (ghorresh kardan)}{غرش کردن (ghorresh kardan)}]{\fa{غرش} \fa{کردن} (ghorresh kardan) — to roar, to rumble (of thunder, a lion, an engine)}

\label{lesson:FA-C475-ghorresh-kardan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a thunderstorm, then the Persian for a lightning strike.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{غرش} \fa{کردن}}
\textbf{\fa{غرش} \fa{کردن}} (\emph{ghorresh kardan}) — \textquotedblleft{}to roar, to rumble (of thunder, a lion, an engine)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{آسمان} \fa{غرش} \fa{کرد} \fa{و} \fa{باران} \fa{شروع} \fa{شد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Âsmân ghorresh kard va bârân shoru' shod.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The sky rumbled and the rain began.
\end{quote}

\emph{ghorresh} 'a roar', from \emph{ghorridan} 'to roar', + \emph{kardan}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{ghorresh kardan} is built from \emph{ghorresh} 'a roar', from \emph{ghorridan} 'to roar', whose origin is not settled, and \emph{kardan} 'to do', inherited from Middle Persian \emph{kardan} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{ghorresh kardan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a thunderstorm, then the Persian for a lightning strike, then say \emph{ghorresh kardan} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{تندباد} (tondbâd)}{تندباد (tondbâd)}]{\fa{تندباد} (tondbâd) — a gale, a strong gust of wind}

\label{lesson:FA-C475-tondbad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a lightning strike, then the Persian for to roar.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{تندباد}}
\textbf{\fa{تندباد}} (\emph{tondbâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a gale, a strong gust of wind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{تندباد} \fa{چند} \fa{درخت} \fa{را} \fa{انداخت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Tondbâd chand derakht râ andâkht.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The gale blew down several trees.
\end{quote}

\emph{tond} 'fast, strong' + \emph{bâd} 'wind'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{tondbâd} is a native compound of \emph{tond} 'fast, violent', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{tund}, and \emph{bâd} 'wind', usually traced to Middle Persian \emph{wād}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tondbâd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{tondbâd}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for a lightning strike, then the Persian for to roar, then say \emph{tondbâd} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{گردباد} (gerdbâd)}{گردباد (gerdbâd)}]{\fa{گردباد} (gerdbâd) — a whirlwind, a tornado}

\label{lesson:FA-C475-gerdbad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to roar, then the Persian for a gale.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{گردباد}}
\textbf{\fa{گردباد}} (\emph{gerdbâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}a whirlwind, a tornado\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{بیابان} \fa{یک} \fa{گردباد} \fa{کوچک} \fa{دیدیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar biyâbân yek gerdbâd-e kuchek didim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We saw a small whirlwind in the desert.
\end{quote}

\emph{gerd} 'round' + \emph{bâd} 'wind'.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gerdbâd} is a native compound of \emph{gerd} 'round', which EtymDB links with PIE \emph{wert-} 'to turn', and \emph{bâd} 'wind'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for to roar, then the Persian for a gale, then say \emph{gerdbâd} again
